Relevance to wounds is now carried by co-location axioms on the wound classes instead of by membership in a causal class.

items.label: Wound healing disorder

parents.label: material disease entity
parents.def: A material entity, part of a human being, that is an abnormal presence or organization of material components — including the limiting case where the abnormal organization consists in a normally-present component being absent — and so has the quality pathological. Which material disease entities compose one disease is fixed by the diagnostic classification assigned to them, not by an intrinsic unity criterion. Identity is grounded in the continuity of the disorder lineage, not in momentary material composition (cf. a river persisting through complete material replacement).

Damaged skin tissue is a wound even while it is still attached, such as necrotic skin; an injury that involves no skin, such as a burn of the inner airways, is no wound.

items.label: Wounds classified according to Gustilo and Anderson

items.label: T drain
items.draft: An abdominal drain consisting of a T-shaped tube whose short crossbar limbs lie in the lumen of the common bile duct and whose long limb leads out through the abdominal wall, bearing a function of draining bile externally.

parents.label: Abdominal drain
parents.def: A drain that is placed in the abdominal cavity or in an abdominal surgical site to carry fluid, blood or air out of the abdomen.

items.label: Impaired wound healing process
items.draft: A wound healing that deviates from the normal orderly and timely sequence of healing phases, such that restoration of tissue integrity is delayed, arrested or yields abnormal tissue.

parents.label: wound healing
parents.def: The series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

items.label: Vancomycin
